programmes.name: Antler Residency — Nordics (Stockholm, Oslo, Copenhagen, Helsinki)
programmes.page_evidence: Application form loads and accepts input (name, email, LinkedIn, stage, region/city) with Stockholm, Oslo, Copenhagen and Helsinki all selectable. Cohort page states: 'Rolling intake: These locations work with founders and teams year-round instead of running fixed residency programs. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis.'
programmes.cohort_dates: Rolling intake year-round across all four Nordic cities; no fixed cohort start dates published. Search reporting (Feb 2026) describes a permanent always-on Nordic residency replacing the old biannual cohorts, with investment decisions in as little as two weeks.
programmes.cash: Reported €500,000 package: €200,000 immediate investment plus €300,000 committed to the next round (ArcticStartup/BeBeez, Feb 2026). NOT stated on antler.co itself — needs verification in phase 2.
programmes.credits_and_tools: Reported $1M+ in partner perks including OpenAI, Anthropic, Perplexity and AWS (secondary source, unverified on antler.co).
programmes.terms_dilution: Equity investment; exact terms not published on the apply page.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Antler's core model is built around individual founders who form teams inside the residency; the apply form accepts a single applicant. Explicitly founder-first rather than team-first.
programmes.location_requirement: Must be able to work from the chosen city. Apply page notes eligibility for multiple locations 'depending on your visa status' — a residence/work permit for the chosen Nordic country is the real gate.
programmes.customer_access: Antler global portfolio and partner network.
programmes.network_quality: Top-tier global pre-seed platform; Nordic partners across four offices.
programmes.brand_value: High — recognisable globally, strong Nordic density.
programmes.application_effort: ~1-2 hours for the basic form; the pitch form additionally takes a deck upload (10MB max). No video required.
programmes.notes: Strongest single fit in this lane: rolling, no entity required, founder-first, and Bangalore is also an Antler location if Nordic visa status blocks. Note Antler is ALSO a recognised Dutch Startup Visa facilitator (listed on RVO), which makes the Amsterdam route a visa path as well as a programme.

programmes.name: Antler Residency — Amsterdam
programmes.page_evidence: Apply form loads with Amsterdam selectable under 'Continental Europe'. Cohort page lists Amsterdam with a start date of September 14, 2026, and states: 'Please note that these are the start dates, not deadlines. We strongly encourage you to apply early to secure a seat.'
programmes.cohort_dates: Cohort start 2026-09-14 (Amsterdam, run jointly with the Germany cohort per the cohort-dates page).
programmes.cash: Reported up to $500K funding with a €2,500/month stipend for the first two months (secondary source: runfutureproof.com). Unverified on antler.co.
programmes.credits_and_tools: Not published on the apply page.
programmes.terms_dilution: Equity; terms not published on the apply page.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Founder-first residency; individual applicants are the norm.
programmes.location_requirement: Amsterdam, in person. Antler states applicants 'must meet visa eligibility requirements for their chosen residency location'.
programmes.customer_access: Antler NL portfolio and partner network; not detailed on the page.
programmes.network_quality: High — Antler NL is one of the most active Dutch pre-seed players.
programmes.application_effort: ~1-2 hours; deck upload optional.
programmes.notes: Antler is on the RVO list of recognised Dutch Startup Visa facilitators, so acceptance here is also a route to a Dutch residence permit. Separate row from the Nordic residency because the format differs (fixed cohort vs rolling intake).

programmes.name: Flagship Accelerator
programmes.region: Estonia (Tallinn) + a second European hub; 80% online
programmes.page_evidence: 'Applications are now open for the program.' and 'applications are checked on first come first serve basis.'
programmes.cohort_dates: 5 months total; 4 modules across weeks 1-14 plus aftercare. Specific cohort start not published on the page.
programmes.cash: Convertible investment up to €100,000, with a further €250,000 follow-on opportunity.
programmes.credits_and_tools: Not published on the programme page.
programmes.terms_dilution: Convertible note; programme cost of €35,000 is netted against the €100,000 investment. Historically ~8% for €50K.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Published requirement of 'at least 2 co-founders/team members'. This is a stated criterion, not a submission gate — the Dealum form will accept a solo submission.
programmes.location_requirement: Hybrid: 80% online, 20% in person in Tallinn and one other European hub. No geographic restriction on applicants; timezone accommodation required.
programmes.customer_access: B2B SaaS focus; corporate and mentor network across 40+ countries.
programmes.network_quality: Strongest B2B SaaS accelerator brand in the Baltics/CEE.
programmes.brand_value: Medium-high in Europe, low in the US.
programmes.application_effort: Dealum form, ~2-3 hours. No video confirmed on the form page.
programmes.notes: Stated criteria also include 'at least a working MVP' and 'initial customer traction, MRR or revenues'. Supaprod has the MVP but zero users and zero revenue — the traction criterion is the real friction here, not the solo-founder line. Focus areas explicitly include 'AI & Automation'.

programmes.name: The Founders Club (Cohort 21)
programmes.page_evidence: 'Applications for the 21st Founders Club cohort are now open until November 2nd.'
programmes.cohort_dates: 3-month online programme; kick-off November 12, graduation presentations February 11.
programmes.cash: Investment offer possible at the end: €100K investment requires a €35K payment from the founder; €50K investment requires €20K. 'If you don't get an investment offer or you decline the offer, you won't be obliged to make any additional payments.'
programmes.credits_and_tools: Not published on the programme page.
programmes.terms_dilution: Entry fee €1,000+VAT for individuals (€1,500+VAT teams, €500+VAT CTOs/developers). Equity only if an investment offer is taken.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Explicitly welcomes solo applicants — 'you can team up with other program participants who have already existing idea propositions'.
programmes.location_requirement: None. Page states no geographical restrictions.
programmes.customer_access: Baltic/CEE B2B network; not detailed on the page.
programmes.network_quality: Good Baltic/CEE B2B network; weaker than the Flagship.
programmes.application_effort: ~2 hours. Prefers B2B tech founders with 7+ years experience or leadership background — the founder's ISRO/Infineon/Intellect arc fits this profile precisely.
programmes.notes: A DIFFERENT Startup Wise Guys programme from the Flagship, with an explicit solo-founder welcome and no traction requirement. Paid entry fee is the main cost.

programmes.name: Innofounder — Round 2 2026
programmes.page_evidence: 'E-grant open for submission of application: from July 28, 2026 to August 25, 2026, at 12:00 PM'
programmes.cohort_dates: 12-month incubator course.
programmes.cash: DKK 27,500 per month for 12 months plus a DKK 100,000 development grant (secondary source); the official page describes three tiers (small/medium/large) based on team size.
programmes.credits_and_tools: Not published on the programme page.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Explicitly welcomes solo: 'You can apply individually or in a team of up to 3 founders.'
programmes.location_requirement: Denmark. 'You must have established a company with a Danish CVR number when the Innofounder process starts' — i.e. at programme start, not at submission.
programmes.customer_access: Danish ecosystem; not detailed on the page.
programmes.network_quality: Danish ecosystem, state-backed.
programmes.application_effort: e-grant.dk submission, likely 8-15 hours. Requires proof of completed higher education.
programmes.hard_blocker: Residence permit not held: 'Non-EU/EEA citizens need a Start-up Denmark visa or Danish education/work history.' The founder is an Indian national in Bangalore with a TUM (German) degree, not Danish. This is a genuine permit wall at application time — but it is unlocked by the separate Startup Denmark scheme listed below, which is itself open on a rolling basis.
programmes.notes: Deadline is 11 days out. The blocker is sequential, not absolute: Startup Denmark approval first, Innofounder second. Not achievable for THIS round; a real target for round 1 2027 if the Danish route is pursued.

programmes.name: Startup Denmark
programmes.page_evidence: 'Self-employed non-EU, non-EEA, and non-Swiss citizens ... can apply with their business plan which is evaluated by an independent expert panel.' The only date caveat on the page is a past one: 'Startup Denmark is closed for evaluations during July. If you submit an application after 14 June 2026, it will be evaluated in August.'
programmes.cohort_dates: Rolling expert-panel evaluation. Residence and work permit granted for up to 2 years, extendable in 3-year blocks.
programmes.cash: None — this is a residence/work permit route, not funding.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Explicitly accepts individuals: 'The scheme can be used by both individuals and teams of up to 3 people.'
programmes.location_requirement: Denmark. 'You must play an active part in running the business ... If you have only economic or financial interests in the business ... you cannot be granted a permit.'
programmes.customer_access: None — government gateway, not a network.
programmes.network_quality: Government gateway rather than a network.
programmes.brand_value: Low as a signal, high as a key — it unlocks Innofounder, Beyond Beta and the wider Danish ecosystem for a non-EU founder.
programmes.application_effort: Business plan submission to the expert panel (est. 15-25 hours), then a separate SIRI permit application with a DKK 1,900 fee and proof of funds for the first year.
programmes.notes: Non-EU nationality is a REQUIREMENT here, not a barrier — the founder qualifies where an EU citizen would not. Quota: maximum 75 foreign nationals granted a permit per calendar year. Evaluated on 4 criteria: innovation, market attractiveness, scalability, team competencies.

programmes.name: Estonian Startup Visa
programmes.page_evidence: Live Dealum application form linked directly from the Startup Estonia page as 'apply for visa'; the page describes a rolling process with no stated deadline.
programmes.cohort_dates: Startup Committee decision typically within 10 working days; visa issued at an embassy thereafter (up to 30 days). Initially 12 months, extendable by six months, then convertible to a temporary residence permit for up to five years.
programmes.cash: None.
programmes.credits_and_tools: Holders get access to e-Residency for remote company management.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: No team-size requirement published.
programmes.location_requirement: Estonia. Company must be 'commencing operations' with an 'innovative and repeatable business model with great global growth potential' and be 'not older than 10 years'.
programmes.customer_access: None directly; gateway to the Estonian ecosystem.
programmes.network_quality: Gateway to the Estonian ecosystem (Startup Wise Guys, Tehnopol, Buildit all sit downstream).
programmes.brand_value: Low as a signal, high as an enabler.
programmes.application_effort: Dealum form plus supporting documents, est. 6-10 hours. State fee €80 for a long-stay D visa, €60 short-stay; no fee for the Startup Committee review itself.
programmes.notes: Criteria state the startup should have 'an MVP and the first traction' — Supaprod has the MVP. Estonia is the cheapest, fastest EU entity+residency combination in this lane and does NOT trip the India/FEMA problem the way an Indian entity would.

programmes.name: Lithuania Startup Visa
programmes.page_evidence: 'If you are startup founder who wish to establish an innovative business in Lithuania, the Startup Visa is a talent attraction scheme that provides a streamlined entry process ... for innovative non-EU entrepreneurs'. Applications are submitted digitally through the Startup Lithuania platform on a rolling basis.
programmes.cohort_dates: Expert panel review ~15-30 days; endorsement letter valid six months; TRP granted initially for up to 2 years, renewable for a further 3.
programmes.cash: None.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: No team-size requirement. Applicant must play an active managerial role.
programmes.location_requirement: Lithuania. UAB incorporation required AFTER endorsement (€1,000 share capital, €250 paid up); founder must have meaningful Lithuanian presence.
programmes.customer_access: Startup Lithuania connects founders to mentors, investors and incubators.
programmes.network_quality: Vilnius fintech/AI cluster; Startup Lithuania is the national ecosystem coordinator.
programmes.application_effort: Business plan in English, est. 10-20 hours. No MVP requirement — 'You do not need a working product before applying.' TRP fees €160 standard / €320 urgent; subsistence proof ~€1,153/month.
programmes.notes: Notably cheaper and faster than the Danish route, and explicitly pre-product friendly. Acceptance into a recognised accelerator (e.g. FIRSTPICK or ROCKIT) strengthens the application.

programmes.name: Residence permit for foreign startups (Startup Visa, facilitator route)
programmes.page_evidence: The RVO page serves a live directory of 30+ approved facilitators (including Antler and Rockstart) with links to each programme page, and describes the ongoing conditions a facilitator must meet. No closure notice.
programmes.cohort_dates: One-year permit, rolling application via IND with RVO assessing the plan.
programmes.cash: None.
programmes.credits_and_tools: None from the state; facilitator provides 'a tailor-made package of support depending on the specific needs of the startup entrepreneur'.
programmes.terms_dilution: None from the state; facilitator terms vary by facilitator.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: No team-size rule published.
programmes.location_requirement: Netherlands. A signed cooperation agreement with a recognised facilitator is mandatory — 'without this cooperation agreement, the application cannot proceed'.
programmes.customer_access: Depends entirely on which facilitator is signed.
programmes.network_quality: Depends entirely on which facilitator is signed.
programmes.application_effort: Step-by-step plan plus proof of funds, est. 10-20 hours, PLUS the separate effort of getting a facilitator to sign.
programmes.notes: Two-sided: the state route is open, but the real gate is a facilitator agreement. Antler and Rockstart are both on the list, so an Antler Amsterdam acceptance solves both problems at once. Worth pursuing as a consequence of an accelerator win rather than as a standalone application.

programmes.name: Slush 100 Startup Competition
programmes.page_evidence: Timeline on the page reads 'Aug 12 – Applications open' and 'Sep 7 – Applications close'; today is 2026-08-14, inside that window. 'The deadline for applications is Sep 7.'
programmes.cohort_dates: Competition runs at Slush, Helsinki (November 2026).
programmes.cash: 'The winner of the Slush 100 competition gets €500,000 with 0% equity from Slush' — the largest equity-free prize in any startup competition.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: No team-size requirement published.
programmes.location_requirement: 'The competition does not have a geographical exclusion.' Attendance in Helsinki required for the competition itself.
programmes.customer_access: Slush audience: thousands of investors and operators.
programmes.network_quality: Very high — Slush is the single densest European founder/investor gathering.
programmes.brand_value: Very high, and the €500K is equity-free.
programmes.application_effort: ~3-5 hours via the Slush platform. Verify whether a video is required in phase 2.
programmes.notes: ENTITY FLAG: the page states eligibility as 'Any startup that has been incorporated during or after 2023' and that has 'raised less than €10,000,000 in equity fundraising'. That wording reads as an incorporation gate at submission — this is the single most important thing to verify in phase 2, because Supaprod has no entity. If the form accepts a pre-incorporation submission, this is the highest-value equity-free target in the entire lane. Deadline is 24 days out.

programmes.name: Slush Startup Stage
programmes.page_evidence: Listed as applications open with 'deadline Aug 31'. 'We give future unicorns 10 minutes to pitch, demo, or do both.'
programmes.cohort_dates: Pitch/demo slot at Slush, Helsinki, November 2026.
programmes.cash: None.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: No team-size requirement published.
programmes.location_requirement: Helsinki attendance for the slot.
programmes.customer_access: Direct stage exposure to the Slush audience.
programmes.network_quality: Very high.
programmes.brand_value: High — a 10-minute demo slot in front of the Slush crowd is a launch moment, and Supaprod's public launch is mid-September 2026, which lines up.
programmes.application_effort: Typeform, likely 1-2 hours.
programmes.notes: Stated target is 'most promising early-stage founders from Seed to Series A', which is a stretch for a pre-revenue product — but this is a stated preference, not a gate. Deadline 17 days out. Lower effort and lower bar than Slush 100; worth filing both.

programmes.name: Sting Core
programmes.page_evidence: Page displays a live 'Apply now' button linking to https://app.sting.co/ and invites applications. CAUTION: the dates rendered on the page are stale — it shows 'Pre-holiday: Dec 14th 2025' and 'Next program start: March 23rd, 2026', while search reporting says the next Sting Core cohort kicks off October 5, 2026 with a mid-August application deadline. The two do not agree.
programmes.cohort_dates: 2 batches per year, up to 12 startups per batch. Conflicting evidence on the next start: page says March 23 2026, secondary reporting says October 5 2026.
programmes.cash: SEK 600,000 convertible note via Propel Capital.
programmes.credits_and_tools: Not published on the programme page.
programmes.terms_dilution: Convertible note plus a Sting 2% warrant.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Published rule: 'A founding team of minimum two people.' A stated criterion, not confirmed as a form-level gate.
programmes.location_requirement: 'Incorporated Swedish AB, team presence in Stockholm during program' — stated as a programme condition. Verify in phase 2 whether the AB must exist to SUBMIT or only to join.
programmes.customer_access: Stockholm corporate and investor network; not detailed on the page.
programmes.network_quality: High in Sweden — Sting is the leading Stockholm accelerator.
programmes.application_effort: Application plus pitch via app.sting.co, est. 4-8 hours.
programmes.notes: Two things to resolve in phase 2: (a) which cohort date is real, since a mid-August deadline would be imminent; (b) whether the Swedish AB requirement bites at submission. Also requires 'Launched MVP and can show traction' — the traction line is the substantive gap. Focus is stated as HealthTech/ClimateTech/DeepTech 'and beyond'.

programmes.name: Norrsken Evolve (formerly Norrsken Impact Accelerator)
programmes.page_evidence: Live 'Apply now' link to an Airtable form; no closure notice on the page. Note that accelerator.norrsken.org now 301-redirects to norrskenevolve.vc — the programme has been rebranded, so older listings describing an '8-week sprint at Norrsken House' for '$125,000 for 7%' may be out of date.
programmes.cohort_dates: Not published on the current page.
programmes.cash: '€250 - €500K equity investment'
programmes.credits_and_tools: Not published on the current page.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not stated on the page.
programmes.location_requirement: 'We primarily support founders from Europe (EU27, EU Candidate Countries and the UK)' but also 'We will support a handful of high-potential companies outside Europe.' A Bangalore-based founder falls into the second category — possible, not preferred.
programmes.customer_access: Norrsken House Stockholm community.
programmes.network_quality: High — Norrsken is a serious European platform with unicorn-founder mentors.
programmes.application_effort: Airtable form, est. 2-4 hours.
programmes.notes: Impact/societal-challenge framing is the main positioning question: Supaprod is a product-development platform, not obviously an impact company. Phase 2 should check whether Evolve has dropped the impact-only mandate along with the rebrand. Contact: hello@norrskenevolve.vc

programmes.name: The Collective (4-month residency) and The Validation Sprint
programmes.page_evidence: Live Typeform application linked from both programme descriptions; no closure notice. Kiuas describes itself as 'a founder collective for ambitious idea-stage builders'.
programmes.cohort_dates: The Collective is a 4-month residency; The Validation Sprint is a 5-week hybrid sprint. No batch dates published on the site.
programmes.cash: None.
programmes.credits_and_tools: 'Building tools worth up to €500k' offered to The Collective participants.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Explicitly welcomes solo — 'You can come as an individual with an idea, or as a team already building.'
programmes.location_requirement: Helsinki for the residency; the Validation Sprint is hybrid. No nationality or incorporation requirement stated.
programmes.customer_access: 'Introductions to investors and operators when you're ready.'
programmes.network_quality: High in Finland — Kiuas is the leading Finnish accelerator and has expanded across the Nordics and Baltics.
programmes.application_effort: Typeform, likely 1-2 hours.
programmes.notes: Free, no equity, solo-welcome, rolling, no entity — one of the lowest-friction rows in the whole lane. Kiuas has restructured since the older 9-week 'Kiuas Accelerator' listings; the current offer is The Collective plus The Validation Sprint. The Collective's stated arc is 'from MVP to €100k MRR', which matches Supaprod's stage.

programmes.name: StartupLab Accelerator
programmes.page_evidence: 'APPLICATIONS FOR ACCELERATOR ARE NOW OPEN' and 'Application deadline is September 25th!'
programmes.cohort_dates: Three-month programme; start date not published on the page.
programmes.cash: 'A 2 to 4 MNOK upfront investment from Startuplab' (approx. €170K-€340K).
programmes.credits_and_tools: Workspace at StartupLab Oslo; not detailed on the page.
programmes.terms_dilution: Targeted ownership around 10%, described as flexible.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: UNRESOLVED — the FAQ literally lists the question 'Do you accept solo founders?' but the answer did not render in the fetch. Worth a direct email in phase 2; the fact that they publish the question at all suggests it is not an automatic no.
programmes.location_requirement: Oslo. Norwegian incorporation requirement not stated on the page; note that Innovation Norway separately allows a Norwegian branch of a foreign company (NUF).
programmes.customer_access: Partner network; not detailed on the page.
programmes.network_quality: High — StartupLab is Norway's leading early-stage incubator and investor.
programmes.brand_value: High in Norway, medium in the wider Nordics.
programmes.application_effort: Online form; they shortlist ~30 companies for interview. Est. 4-6 hours.
programmes.notes: Stated criteria: pre-seed or early-stage, scalable tech, global ambitions, 'launched or planning launch within six months'. Supaprod's mid-September public launch fits that window exactly. Cheque size is the largest of any open accelerator in this lane. Deadline 42 days out.

programmes.name: Start it @KBC — Fall 2026
programmes.region: Belgium (Antwerp, Brussels, Ghent, Hasselt, Leuven, Kortrijk)
programmes.page_evidence: 'Applications for Fall 2026 are open!' with a deadline of '14.09.2026'
programmes.cohort_dates: Start 28.10.2026 following a mandatory two-day bootcamp; 12-month programme; 24h/month time commitment; 65 selected participants.
programmes.cash: None from the accelerator itself. Separately, the new €100M Start it Fund invests on average €300,000 at early stage.
programmes.credits_and_tools: Not published on the programme page.
programmes.terms_dilution: 'FREE' and '100% no strings attached' — 'we don't ask for shares, money or special privileges.' Equity only if the separate Start it Fund invests.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: No team-size requirement published. The page states they seek 'enthusiastic & open-minded founders of all backgrounds, genders, ages and nationalities.'
programmes.location_requirement: Belgium hubs plus Budapest and a New York presence. 24h/month commitment implies regular presence; whether that can be remote is unverified.
programmes.customer_access: KBC corporate network and Global Accelerator Network membership.
programmes.network_quality: Strong in Belgium; 1,900+ startups supported since 2014.
programmes.application_effort: AcceleratorApp form, est. 3-5 hours.
programmes.notes: Equity-free, nationality-agnostic wording, no entity requirement found, deadline 31 days out. One of the cleanest Benelux fits. The 24h/month commitment over 12 months is the real cost to weigh against a Nordic residency.

programmes.name: Founder Institute — Nordics Fall 2026
programmes.page_evidence: 'Applications are now open' with 'Early Deadline: Sep 1, 2026'
programmes.cohort_dates: Programme runs Nov 27, 2026 – Feb 05, 2027. 'This program will contain required sessions that are both online and in-person.'
programmes.cash: None.
programmes.terms_dilution: Paid: 'Early Entrance Fee $799' (regular $1299). FI historically also takes a small equity/warrant stake — verify in phase 2.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Built for individual founders; the form's stage options run from 'Entrepreneur with just an idea/Aspiring Entrepreneur' upward.
programmes.location_requirement: Hybrid, Nordics-based sessions. Verify whether the in-person requirement can be met remotely from Bangalore.
programmes.customer_access: Global mentor network; no customer channel.
programmes.network_quality: Medium — broad global mentor network, thinner signal than the top accelerators.
programmes.brand_value: Low-medium. FI is not a differentiating credential at Supaprod's stage.
programmes.application_effort: ~1-2 hours.
programmes.notes: Lowest-signal row on this list and it costs money rather than paying it. Included for completeness; deprioritise against Kiuas, StartupLab and Antler, which are all free or paying.

programmes.name: FIRSTPICK Accelerator
programmes.page_evidence: Application form loads fully with multiple required fields. The 'Where are you based?' dropdown includes 'Outside of Europe', and the 'When was your startup incorporated?' dropdown includes 'Not incorporated yet' — both directly relevant. No deadline or closure notice on the page.
programmes.cohort_dates: Batches run periodically (Batch 6 documented), but the firm states it 'invests year-round, not just during accelerator cycles.'
programmes.cash: €100K to €500K initial cheque, follow-on capacity up to €1M. Second fund is €25M, launched 2026.
programmes.credits_and_tools: Not published on the apply page.
programmes.terms_dilution: Not published on the apply page.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not stated. The fund's public thesis is backing 'founders who may be overlooked by traditional VC criteria' — which reads favourably for a solo, non-EU applicant.
programmes.location_requirement: Baltic focus in the branding, but the form explicitly accepts applicants based outside Europe.
programmes.customer_access: Backed by Lithuania's Ministry of Economy, the ILTE fund, and founders from Tesonet, Oberlo and Kilo Health.
programmes.network_quality: Strong in the Baltics; targeting AI-first software, which is Supaprod's category.
programmes.application_effort: ~1-2 hours. 'they reply to every founder within 48 hours' — fastest feedback loop in this lane.
programmes.notes: The single most permissive form found in this sweep: it names 'Not incorporated yet' and 'Outside of Europe' as valid answers, which resolves both of the founder's usual objections before they are raised. Rolling, fast, and thesis-aligned on AI-first software.

programmes.name: Beyond Beta — Batch #15
programmes.page_evidence: 'The application round for Batch #15 opens on August 10, 2026.' No closing date published on the page; today is 2026-08-14, so the round opened four days ago.
programmes.cohort_dates: 12-month programme of workshops, camps and 1:1 mentor sparring.
programmes.cash: None — the programme itself is the benefit.
programmes.terms_dilution: 'free to participate in as it is EU-funded'.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Requires 'a committed founder team' — wording implies a team but does not publish a minimum number.
programmes.location_requirement: Denmark.
programmes.customer_access: Danish industry clusters (life science, robotics, sound) and investor network.
programmes.network_quality: Medium-high in Denmark; '60% of Beyond Beta alumni have raised funding'.
programmes.application_effort: Est. 4-8 hours.
programmes.hard_blocker: Danish CVR number required at submission: 'The CVR-number of the company may not be older than 7 years, when you submit your application' — this presupposes a CVR exists at submission time, unlike Innofounder which only requires one at programme start.
programmes.notes: Free and open right now, but the CVR-at-submission wording is a genuine entity gate. Sequenced behind Startup Denmark + Danish incorporation. Phase 2 should confirm whether the form actually rejects a blank CVR field.

programmes.name: Luxembourg-City Incubator
programmes.organisation: Luxembourg Chamber of Commerce / House of Startups
programmes.page_evidence: Apply page serves a live three-step process: 'Complete the application form', 'Get invited for a selection interview', 'Join the next cohort and start your journey.' No closure notice and no published deadline.
programmes.cohort_dates: Cohort-based but dates not published.
programmes.cash: None published.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not stated.
programmes.location_requirement: Luxembourg City.
programmes.customer_access: Chamber of Commerce network.
programmes.network_quality: Medium; the main value is as a Luxembourg landing pad and a Fit 4 Start feeder.
programmes.application_effort: Unknown; form not inspected. Contact info@cityincubator.lu / +352 28 81 01 01.
programmes.notes: Six stated focus areas — Environment, Urban Technology, Construction and Real Estate, Commerce, Tourism, Logistics — none of which is a developer-tools/AI platform. Sector fit is the weak point, not eligibility. Chiefly useful as a route into the Luxembourg ecosystem ahead of the next Fit 4 Start call.

programmes.name: Accelerator Program (Accelerate)
programmes.page_evidence: Live 'Apply now' button on the join-as-startup page with no closure notice; the page invites applications and lists three programme tracks (Validate, Accelerate, Deep-dive).
programmes.cohort_dates: Accelerator is a 3-month programme; cohort dates not published on the page.
programmes.cash: None — this is a paid programme.
programmes.credits_and_tools: Workspace and TU Delft facilities access.
programmes.terms_dilution: 'YES!Delft takes no equity.' Participation fee €3,500 (excl. VAT) per team, plus a €25,000 (excl. VAT) success fee payable only on reaching €1M additional annual revenue or €1M total funding.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Published 2+ rule: 'Minimum co-founders: at least two required' — but the page explicitly offers solo founders a route in, noting solo founders 'can join a workshop to find a co-founder'. That is a documented on-ramp, not a rejection.
programmes.location_requirement: 'Based in or moving to The Netherlands.' No TU Delft affiliation needed — 'You do not need to be a TU Delft student, alumnus, or staff member.'
programmes.customer_access: TU Delft ecosystem, 560+ deeptech alumni.
programmes.network_quality: High for deeptech in NL.
programmes.application_effort: Est. 3-5 hours.
programmes.notes: Deeptech-leaning; an AI product-development platform is a plausible but not obvious fit. The relocation requirement is the practical gate and connects back to the Dutch Startup Visa row. Equity-free with a deferred success fee is an unusually founder-friendly structure.

programmes.name: Venture Building Program — Fall Cohort 2026
programmes.page_evidence: Page is actively recruiting for the Fall Cohort 2026 with a live 'Apply now' control; FAQ answers current applicant questions. No closure notice.
programmes.cohort_dates: 12-month Venture Building Program; Fall 2026 cohort. Monthly in-person sprint weeks are mandatory.
programmes.cash: 'Do I get paid to be in the Program? No, you will not be paid to join the HighTechXL Program.' but 'There will be possibilities for remuneration via investments and subsidies.'
programmes.credits_and_tools: High Tech Campus Eindhoven facilities (building HTC 27).
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Individual co-founders are the intended intake — HighTechXL actively recruits solo entrepreneurs to match against technologies ('Co-founders Wanted').
programmes.location_requirement: 'I don't live in Eindhoven. Can I still join the Program? Yes, you can join the HighTechXL Program from anywhere in the Netherlands.' — Netherlands residence is implied.
programmes.customer_access: Deep-tech corporate ecosystem around the High Tech Campus (ASML, Philips orbit).
programmes.network_quality: High for hardware/deeptech, low relevance for software.
programmes.application_effort: Co-founder questionnaire, then intro meeting, 1-1 interview, and a final technical interview. Est. 3-5 hours of writing plus interview time.
programmes.notes: Model mismatch worth naming: HighTechXL primarily matches founders TO licensed hard technologies rather than accelerating a founder's own software product. Included for lane completeness; low fit for Supaprod. Contact entrepreneur@hightechxl.com

programmes.name: Startup Highway (pre-acceleration and incubation)
programmes.page_evidence: 'ROCKIT programs never stop, and there's no better time than now to join our Startup Highway!' — the page invites applications on an ongoing basis with no closure notice.
programmes.cohort_dates: Continuous: hackathons, pre-acceleration and incubation programmes. The separate ROCKIT Impact Accelerator is a 4-month programme taking 6 startups per batch.
programmes.cash: None — support is delivered as de minimis state aid (EU cap €200,000 over three fiscal years).
programmes.credits_and_tools: ROCKIT office membership in Kaunas and Klaipėda; free consultations with market experts and mentors; consultations on company establishment.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not stated.
programmes.location_requirement: HARD: 'Your company should be based in Central or Western Lithuania (Kaunas-Klaipėda).' Plus 'The company must have been established within the last five years.'
programmes.customer_access: B2B partners offered as first customers and pilots — genuinely useful for a zero-customer product.
programmes.network_quality: Medium; strong in Lithuanian fintech and sustainability.
programmes.application_effort: Contact-form led ('Drop us a line, and we'll find the best fit'). Low effort to start.
programmes.hard_blocker: Requires an existing company based specifically in Central or Western Lithuania (Kaunas-Klaipėda corridor) — both an entity and a sub-national location gate.
programmes.notes: Stated interest areas include AI, which fits. But the regional incorporation requirement makes this a downstream option only if the Lithuania Startup Visa route is taken AND the UAB is registered outside Vilnius. Their B2B-partner-as-first-customer offer is the most directly relevant benefit in this lane for a product with zero users.

programmes.name: Maria 01 campus membership
programmes.page_evidence: Page invites applications on a rolling basis: 'Joining the Maria 01 Community starts with sending an application' via the application form. No closure notice.
programmes.cohort_dates: Not cohort-based; selection-based campus membership.
programmes.cash: None — this is paid workspace plus community.
programmes.credits_and_tools: Co-working from €150/month + VAT; dedicated desks with 24/7 access; offices from €250/person.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Fresh Membership tier exists 'for those exploring a business idea', which accommodates a solo pre-entity founder.
programmes.location_requirement: Helsinki campus.
programmes.customer_access: ~200 active startups on campus; nearly 600 since 2016 have raised over €1 billion collectively.
programmes.network_quality: High density in Finland — the Nordics' largest startup campus.
programmes.brand_value: Low as a credential, high as a base.
programmes.application_effort: ~1 hour.
programmes.notes: Not an accelerator and offers no capital, so it competes for none of the same slots. Its value is as a physical landing pad if the Finnish/Slush route is pursued. Include only as a supporting move.

programmes.name: GründerAcademy
programmes.page_evidence: Direct WebFetch of https://www.thefactory.no/grunder-academy returned HTTP 404, and the alternate path /grunderacademy also failed. Cached content retrieved via a secondary tool shows 'Application Deadline: 1. september' alongside 'Program start: September 2025', which is a stale page snapshot — the September deadline may refer to 2025, not 2026. I could not load the live page to confirm either the deadline or whether the form accepts input.
programmes.cohort_dates: 12 weeks, twice per year (spring and autumn), 70-80 startups per year across four Norwegian regions.
programmes.cash: None — 'a free 3-month accelerator program'.
programmes.terms_dilution: Free; TheFactory invests separately through its funds.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not stated.
programmes.location_requirement: 'targeting Norwegian startups within fintech, proptech, retail, saas/business, and impact' — Norwegian company almost certainly required. Sponsored by SpareBank 1 Sør-Norge and delivered regionally.
programmes.customer_access: 120+ mentor network.
programmes.network_quality: Medium-high in Norway; nominated for Best Accelerator at the Nordic Startup Awards 2026.
programmes.application_effort: Unknown.
programmes.hard_blocker: none established — the Norwegian-startup targeting is a stated focus, not a confirmed eligibility wall
programmes.notes: The 'saas/business' vertical fits Supaprod, but the programme is explicitly aimed at Norwegian startups. Phase 2 must load the live page (try thefactory.no directly and follow the 'Learn More & Apply' link from the homepage) to establish both the real deadline and whether non-Norwegian applicants are accepted. TheFactory also runs a DefSec accelerator (start March 23, 2026) and a Sportstech Academy, both clear vertical mismatches and excluded here.

programmes.name: Katapult Accelerator
programmes.page_evidence: Direct WebFetch of https://katapult.vc/ returned HTTP 403 Forbidden — the site blocked automated retrieval, so I could not see whether an application is open or whether a form loads. This is a bot-block, not a closure signal.
programmes.cohort_dates: 3-month programme, reported as fully digital ('you won't have to relocate to Oslo to participate').
programmes.cash: Reported €150,000-€500,000 investments (secondary sources).
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not established.
programmes.location_requirement: None per secondary reporting — the programme is digital.
programmes.customer_access: 130+ startups since 2017, including two unicorns (Esusu, Betterfly).
programmes.network_quality: High for impact tech.
programmes.application_effort: Online application then several interviews.
programmes.notes: Focus is climate change and ocean conservation impact startups, plus a stated requirement to have 'already proven their product-market fit with some form of validation'. Both are poor fits for Supaprod. Retained as a row because the 403 means I have no page-based evidence either way, and the fully-digital format would otherwise be attractive. Phase 2 should retry via a browser tool rather than WebFetch.

programmes.name: AI Accelerator (AI-kiirendi)
programmes.page_evidence: 'Kandideerimine avaneb 24. augustil' (Applications open August 24th). The registration window is stated as 24 August – 25 September 2026. As of today, 2026-08-14, the form is not yet live; the page offers only a 'Registreeri huvi' (Register interest) button.
programmes.cohort_dates: 6-month accelerator, Fall 2026 cohort.
programmes.cash: €10,000 development grants awarded to up to 3 companies by the expert panel at demo day.
programmes.terms_dilution: 'Program participation itself is free with no equity taken.'
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not stated; requires 'motiveeritud ja vajalike oskustega tiim' (a motivated team with the necessary skills).
programmes.location_requirement: 'Eestis registreeritud ettevõte' — an Estonian-registered company is required.
programmes.customer_access: Estonian AI and enterprise network.
programmes.network_quality: Medium.
programmes.application_effort: Unknown until the form opens on Aug 24.
programmes.notes: Opens in 10 days and is squarely on-thesis: a scalable AI-based business idea with an existing prototype is the stated requirement, and Supaprod meets it. The Estonian entity requirement is real but cheap to satisfy via e-Residency plus an OÜ — far cheaper than the Danish or Swedish equivalents. Register interest now so the opening is not missed.

programmes.name: imec.istart Belgium — Autumn 2026 call
programmes.page_evidence: The apply page lists Belgium Autumn 2026 as 'Open call Sept 1 - Sept 30 (midnight)' and offers only a 'NOTIFY ME' option — the call is not yet open as of 2026-08-14.
programmes.cohort_dates: Business support programme of minimum 12 months. Three open calls per year.
programmes.cash: €100,000 via convertible loan plus full in-kind support, with up to €300,000 available in future rounds.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Stated criteria ask for 'a complementary team' — a preference, not a published minimum.
programmes.location_requirement: International startups from the EU 'need to establish a branch office in Flanders or conclude a cooperation with a knowledge institute in Flanders'. Note this wording is EU-scoped; whether a non-EU founder qualifies is unresolved and is the key phase-2 question.
programmes.customer_access: imec's nano-electronics and digital tech ecosystem.
programmes.network_quality: High — described as Europe's number 1 university-linked accelerator.
programmes.brand_value: High in Benelux and European deeptech.
programmes.application_effort: Application documents are downloadable in advance from the apply page — worth pulling now to draft ahead of Sept 1. Est. 6-10 hours.
programmes.hard_blocker: none confirmed — but the Flanders branch-office / knowledge-institute cooperation requirement for non-Belgian applicants needs resolving in phase 2
programmes.notes: Opens in 18 days. Stated criteria are 'developing a tech product', 'a complementary team', 'a working proof of concept' — Supaprod clears the product and PoC bars. Teams may apply a maximum of 2 times, so do not burn an attempt on a weak submission.

programmes.name: imec.istart Netherlands — Autumn 2026 call
programmes.page_evidence: The apply page lists The Netherlands Autumn 2026 as 'Open call Oct 1 - Oct 31' with only a 'NOTIFY ME' option — the call is not yet open as of 2026-08-14.
programmes.cohort_dates: Minimum 12-month support programme.
programmes.cash: €100,000 convertible loan (per the Belgian programme terms; NL terms not separately published).
programmes.solo_founder_stance: 'a complementary team' preferred.
programmes.location_requirement: Netherlands. The Flanders branch-office rule applies to the Belgian track; the NL equivalent is unpublished.
programmes.customer_access: imec ecosystem.
programmes.network_quality: High.
programmes.application_effort: Est. 6-10 hours; templates downloadable now.
programmes.notes: A DIFFERENT geographic track of the same organisation, opening a month after the Belgian one — which means a Belgian rejection in September does not preclude an NL submission in October, subject to the 'maximum 2 applications' rule. Worth confirming in phase 2 whether the two-attempt cap is per-country or global.

programmes.name: Fit 4 Start (call #17 closed; #18 expected)
programmes.page_evidence: 'The call for applications for Fit 4 Start #17 is now closed.' The call closed Friday 10 July 2026 with 556 applications received. No date is published for call #18.
programmes.cohort_dates: Not published for the next call.
programmes.cash: 'Up to €150,000 of equity-free funding'
programmes.credits_and_tools: Coaching plus support from Technoport, the Luxembourg Space Agency, Luxembourg City Incubator, LHoFT and LuxProvide.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Published rule: 'Team composed of at least 2 people'. Per the binding rules this is one condition and not a stop, but it is an explicit published minimum rather than a soft preference.
programmes.location_requirement: Luxembourg. Verticals for the last call were digital, health technologies, space, and a new defence vertical.
programmes.customer_access: Luxembourg financial and space ecosystem.
programmes.network_quality: Medium-high; €150K equity-free is among the largest non-dilutive cheques in the lane.
programmes.application_effort: Est. 10-15 hours.
programmes.notes: Genuinely closed right now, but this is a recurring twice-yearly call — set a watch for #18 rather than dropping it. The digital vertical is the fit. Also worth monitoring events.luxinnovation.lu for the next call announcement.

programmes.name: Innovative Startups 2026 (Innovativa Startups)
programmes.page_evidence: 'We are updating the process for the call for proposals. Therefore, we have postponed the opening date to October 12th.' The call 'Opens on 12 October 2026' and closes '12 Jan 2027 at 14:00'. Not open as of 2026-08-14.
programmes.cohort_dates: Not a cohort programme; project grant.
programmes.cash: 'Maximum SEK 500,000' (approx. €43,000).
programmes.solo_founder_stance: No team-size requirement.
programmes.location_requirement: 'Swedish limited liability companies that are no more than 10 years old, have a maximum of 10 employees' — a Swedish AB is the applicant entity.
programmes.customer_access: None — this is money, not network.
programmes.network_quality: Low — this is money, not network.
programmes.application_effort: Est. 15-25 hours in the Vinnova eServices portal, in a two-step process.
programmes.hard_blocker: A Swedish AB must be the applicant. The applicant is the company, not the founder, so no entity means no submission.
programmes.notes: Opens in 59 days and closes five months later — a long runway if a Swedish AB is ever created. Deprioritise unless the Sting Core route makes a Swedish AB worthwhile anyway, in which case these two stack.

programmes.name: Tempo funding
programmes.page_evidence: 'The Tempo funding application period has closed in October 2025 for the time being.' and 'The Tempo application period closes on 3.10.2025 at 23.59 for the year 2025.' The closure is attributed to the funding authorisation situation.
programmes.cohort_dates: Not applicable.
programmes.cash: 'The maximum amount of Tempo funding is EUR 60,000.'
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Requires 'a committed team of at least 2 people working in Finland. Individuals must already be working for the company when applying for funding.'
programmes.location_requirement: Finland. Applicant must be a Finnish limited liability company in operation for less than five years.
programmes.customer_access: None.
programmes.network_quality: Low.
programmes.application_effort: Est. 15-25 hours.
programmes.hard_blocker: Closed since October 2025 with no reopening date published, plus a Finnish limited company and a 2-person Finland-based team requirement.
programmes.notes: Recorded to close the loop on the lane brief. Do not spend effort here without a fresh reopening announcement; Finnish innovation funding took drastic state budget cuts.

programmes.name: NIY funding (Young Innovative Company)
programmes.page_evidence: I did not load the NIY programme page itself — my only evidence is a Business Finland news page summarised via search, which stated that 'The NIY funding for the growth and internationalization of startup companies will most likely remain closed, due to drastic cuts to innovation funding in the state budget.' Hedged wording on a secondary page is not a closure notice on the programme page, so I am not recording this as CLOSED.
programmes.cohort_dates: Three milestone-gated phases.
programmes.cash: Up to €1 million per company across three phases, milestone-contingent.
programmes.terms_dilution: Non-dilutive grant, but requires 50% company co-funding of total project costs in each phase.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not stated.

programmes.customer_access: None.
programmes.network_quality: Low.

programmes.hard_blocker: none confirmed; the 50% co-funding requirement is the practical barrier
programmes.notes: The 50% co-funding requirement blocks this regardless of open status: €250,000 of Business Finland money requires €250,000 of the founder's own or investor capital in the same phase. Phase 2 should load the page itself before ruling either way.

programmes.name: Grants for Market Clarification / Commercialisation phase 1 and 2

ID-porten is Norway's national electronic ID, which requires a Norwegian national identity number to obtain. I could not reach the form to see whether it accepts input, so this is a login wall, not a closure.
programmes.cohort_dates: Not cohort-based; rolling assessment.
programmes.cash: Market Clarification reported at up to NOK 150,000 covering 100% of costs (secondary source: PNO Innovation). Not confirmed on innovasjonnorge.no itself.
programmes.solo_founder_stance: Not stated.
programmes.location_requirement: Norway. Notably, 'Registered Norwegian Branches of Foreign Companies (NUF) have the opportunity to apply, provided their operations and projects are situated within Norway' — a branch, not a full subsidiary, may suffice.
programmes.customer_access: None — state funding body.
programmes.network_quality: Low — state funding body.
programmes.application_effort: Unknown; a common application template covers several schemes. There is also a 'rapid assessment tool' at raskavklaring.innovasjonnorge.no which may be reachable without ID-porten.
programmes.hard_blocker: none confirmed; the ID-porten login requires a Norwegian national identity number, which is a practical barrier for a non-resident
programmes.notes: The NUF branch route is the interesting detail: it could let a foreign parent apply without a full Norwegian AS. Phase 2 should try raskavklaring.innovasjonnorge.no and email kundesupport@innovasjonnorge.no rather than fighting the portal.

A direct WebFetch returned HTTP 403; content was retrieved via a secondary fetch tool.
